hypothesis: The ID/EX payload (the operand+immediate payload of the pipeline register) is not being captured correctly in id_stage, so EX executes every instruction with a zeroed B operand and a mis-sliced immediate — while control fields (alu_op, branch, jump, reg_write) are fine, so the ALU opcode itself is correct and the failures are silent, per-opcode value errors rather than global breakage. Two concrete mechanisms, both inside the ID/EX register block of id_stage: (1) id_ex_rs2_data is effectively a constant 0 / is never loaded from rs2_data, so every R-type op computes rs1 <op> 0 — OR x4 gives rs1 alone (0xb -> 0x3), SLT/SLTU x16/x17 give 0, and the t05_forward chain degenerates into `result = rs1`, so each register ends up holding the previous chain value (x2=0x5=x1, x3=0xf=x2_old, x5=0xa, x13=0x2a), exactly the 'forwarding looks broken but is actually never needed' signature; (2) id_ex_imm for I-type takes the slice {instr[31:21],1'b0} zero-extended instead of sign-extended instr[31:20], so ADDI -2049 (0xFFFFF7FF) yields 0x000007FE. The same zeroed/corrupted operands feed the EX branch comparator, so loops in bench_ooo_overlap64 never take the exit branch, PC keeps walking dmem reads (0xc24..0xc5c) until the 6000-cycle timeout and the ECALL never retires, leaving halted=0. constraints: Do not change any module port names, widths or directions frozen in the interface contract (id_stage, ex_stage and all 8 modules keep their existing ports).
id_ex_* outputs must remain registered (a pipeline register clocked by clk), loaded only when the ID stage advances; on rst_n=0 all id_ex_valid/id_ex control must clear to 0.

Keep the forwarding contract intact: forwarding_unit unchanged in behaviour, EX/MEM -> EX has priority over MEM/WB -> EX, forward is suppressed when ex_mem_rd_addr==0, mem_wb_rd_addr==0 or the source register field is x0.
ALU B mux semantics must stay: R-type/I-type ALU ops use id_ex_imm when id_ex_alu_b_sel==1 and id_ex_rs2_data when 0; do not invert the polarity as a workaround.

Immediate generation: I-type = sign-extended instr[31:20]; S-type = {instr[31:25],instr[11:7]}; B-type = {instr[31],instr[7],instr[30:25],instr[11:8],1'b0} sign-extended; U-type = {instr[31:12],12'b0}; J-type per spec. No zero-extension, no
Do not touch load-use stall, redirect/flush timing, halt/halted WB-only semantics, dmem_valid rst_n/halted masking, or the single-cycle memory model.
No hardcoded test values, no per-opcode special cases keyed to the testbench, no disabling of checks or debug flags.
verification_targets: t03_alu_imm: x3 must become 0xfffff7ff (currently 0x000007fe) — proves I-type immediate is sign-extended from instr[31:20] with bit0 intact.
t02_alu_r: x4 must become 0x0000000b (currently 0x00000003), x16 and x17 must both become 0x00000001 (currently 0) — proves the R-type B operand is the real rs2, not 0.

t05_forward: x2=0x0000000f, x3=0x00000014, x4=0x0000001e, x5=0x0000000f, x7=0x00000002, x13=0x00000054 (currently 0x5/0xf/0xf/0xa/0x14/0x2a) — proves both EX/MEM and MEM/WB forwarding deliver the producer value.
bench_ooo_overlap64: halted must assert with exit_code=0 well before max_cycles=6000, and the PC must leave 0x00000028 instead of scanning dmem 0xc24..0xc5c forever.
Suite totals: base and performance_correctness must report 0 failures (currently 58 failures / 291617 checks) with the RV32I capability check no longer at verified=-1.
